description: Issue #838 AC5, the profile-blind half — and the fixture whose ABSENCE let a real defect ship. `ol-duplicate-definition` is not gated on any profile: `spec/execution-model.md:82-88` makes phase-1 registration unconditional ("The reader registers every `define`/`to` procedure **and every `struct` declaration** … a name an earlier declaration in the program or an imported module already registered raises `ol-duplicate-definition`"), and `spec/data-structures.md:304` says the same of a struct type name. Note the profile set here is **`core-language` alone, with `data` absent**, while every `struct` below still participates. That is the whole point: a profile decides whether a name *works*, never whether a program may declare it (`spec/grammar.md:408`), and `@openlogo/runtime`'s own phase-1 guard is profile-blind, so gating the checker made `check()` and `execute()` disagree — a Core-only program ran into a runtime error the checker had just called clean, which is the disagreement `docs/design-notes/0007-binding-vs-registration.md` says this ruling removes. The first round of #838 DID gate it on `data` (by false analogy with issue #405, which reasoned about what a declaration *registers* rather than what the program *declares*), and it survived every gate: the only duplicate-definition fixtures lived under `tests/conformance/data/`, so the corpus directory pinned the profile set and the profile-blind half was never exercised. Its sibling `declare-built-in-names-core-only` is the same guard for `ol-reserved-word`; this file is the one AC5 was missing. What the program pins, line by line: line 2 is a struct duplicating a struct (original line 1); line 6 is a struct duplicating a define (original line 3); and line 7 is a define duplicating that SAME line-3 define, with a struct declaration sitting between them. That third row is a third declaration of one name across mixed kinds, so its original_span must be line 3 and NOT line 6 -- and it is the regression guard for the second defect this issue's first round shipped: a separate map per declaration kind, consulted procedures-first, pointed the third declaration at the second. Both defects, the profile gate and the per-kind maps, are fixed by ONE first-declaration map shared by both kinds; this file fails if either returns. This is a check-mode fixture: nothing is executed and no events are produced.
